chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Bunān ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from al-Sakūnī, from Jaʿfar, from his father, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
“Whoever dies in the crowd of Friday, or ʿArafah, or on a bridge, and they do not know who killed him, then his blood-money is upon the Bayt al-Mal.”

key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَالِ: the public treasury responsible for communal financial obligations
key_terms.جُمُعَةٍ: the Friday gathering or Friday prayer occasion
key_terms.جِسْرٍ: a bridge where such a death may occur
key_terms.زِحَامِ: a dense crowd or crush of people
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: the standing place/time of ʿArafah during hajj

ai.seo_question: Who pays the diyah for someone killed in a crowd when the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person killed in a crowded place when the killer is unknown. It states that the diyah is to be paid from the Bayt al-Mal, establishing public financial responsibility in cases where no individual perpetrator can be identified.
